History with other complex systems shows that without constraints, complexity can lead to instability.

However, if "self-improvement" means allowing an AI to iteratively learn from data, refine its reasoning, and adapt to new environments, then **blocking it is a mistake**. AI needs to be able to improve within safe boundaries. Total restriction stifles innovation, prevents useful applications, and can actually make systems less robust by limiting their exposure to diverse, real-world scenarios. The goal isn't to stop improvement; it's to guide it responsibly.
